University enrollment climbs toward a thousand, 1905–1914 · Storyline · Orange County Indexed

# University enrollment climbs toward a thousand, 1905–1914

University enrollment climbed from 512 in 1900 toward 1,000 by December 1914, when Edward Kidder Graham told the trustees it would pass that mark, and the campus grew from ten buildings to two dozen. In October 1905 a freshman class of 200 was reported as the largest in the University's history, and the spring term of 1908 enrolled 770, a record by the News's account. In January 1909 President Francis P. Venable reported nearly 800 students to the trustees, about 92 percent from North Carolina, and an increase in the annual appropriation was asked. By September 1912 nearly 800 had enrolled, and more than 100 applicants had been turned away as not prepared to enter.

In October 1905 the university's fall enrollment ran 60 ahead of the year before, and its freshman class of 200 was reported as the largest in its history; President Francis P. Venable called them as fine a set of young men as he had seen. The spring term that opened in the first week of January 1908 enrolled 770, which the News said was the largest in the university's history. On January 22, 1909 Venable reported enrollment of nearly 800 to the trustees, about 92 percent from North Carolina, with Orange County sending 33 students, the most of any county. The trustees were told the year's resources came to $150,623.74 against $147,190.46 spent, and an increase of $30,000 in the annual appropriation was asked. The university began its 120th year on September 12, 1912 with chapel in Gerrard Hall for some 500 returning and 250 new students. By the next week nearly 800 had enrolled, and more than 100 applicants had been turned away as not prepared to enter. In December 1914 Edward Kidder Graham told the trustees that enrollment would pass 1,000, against 512 in 1900, and that counting summer students the university taught 1,578. The campus had grown from ten buildings in 1900 to two dozen.

## The events, date by date

Every statement above comes from these dated entries in the chronology. Each links to its source.

1. by October 26, 1905

Statistic or record · University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill The university enrolls its largest freshman class

The university's fall enrollment ran 60 ahead of the year before, and its freshman class of 200 was reported as the largest in its history; President Francis P. Venable called them as fine a set of young men as he had seen.

 Orange County Observer (Hillsborough), October 26, 1905, p. 2 In the chronology 
2. early January 1908

Statistic or record · University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill The university opens its spring term with a record 770 students

The university's spring term opened in the first week of January with an enrollment of 770, which the News said was the largest in its history.

 The News (Chapel Hill), January 16, 1908, p. 1 In the chronology 
3. January 22, 1909

Statistic or record · University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill Venable reports university enrollment near 800, with Orange sending the most students

President Venable's report to the university trustees put enrollment at nearly 800, about 92 percent from North Carolina, with Orange County sending 33 students, the most of any county. The trustees were told resources for the year came to $150,623.74 against $147,190.46 spent, and an increase of $30,000 in the annual appropriation was asked.

 Orange County Observer (Hillsborough), January 28, 1909, p. 4 In the chronology 
4. September 12, 1912

Statistic or record · Gerrard Hall, UNC campus, Chapel Hill The university opens its 120th year with nearly 800 students

The university began its 120th year with chapel in Gerrard Hall for some 500 returning and 250 new students. By the next week nearly 800 had enrolled, and more than 100 applicants were turned away as not prepared to enter.

 The News (Chapel Hill), September 19, 1912, p. 5 In the chronology 
5. December 1914

Statistic or record · UNC, Chapel Hill Graham reports enrollment passing 1,000 students

Graham told the trustees in December 1914 that enrollment would pass 1,000, against 512 in 1900, and that counting summer students the university taught 1,578. The campus had grown from ten buildings in 1900 to two dozen.
